Name: creative_limits_lms
Title: Exploring Creative Limits of Language Models through Multi-Token Prediction and Seed-Conditioning
Short Hypothesis: This research investigates whether multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning enhance the algorithmic creativity of language models by allowing them to perform open-ended tasks requiring a leap of thought, compared to traditional next-token prediction.
Related Work: Existing studies have shown that multi-token prediction (MTP) can enhance language models' performance in various tasks. However, little work has focused on quantifying the creative limits of LLMs specifically in open-ended tasks that require abstract reasoning and planning. This proposal distinguishes itself by introducing a novel test-bed of tasks and the concept of seed-conditioning, which has not been thoroughly explored in this context.
Abstract: This research introduces a controlled set of minimal algorithmic tasks that evaluate the creative limits of large language models (LLMs). These tasks require a stochastic planning step that either discovers novel connections in knowledge graphs or constructs new patterns, simulating open-ended real-world challenges. We propose that traditional next-token learning is myopic, whereas multi-token prediction (MTP) approaches, such as teacherless training and diffusion models, excel in producing diverse and original outputs. Our novel seed-conditioning technique, which introduces randomness at the input layer, is presented as an effective method to elicit creativity without sacrificing coherence, performing comparably to existing output-layer temperature sampling. This study aims to provide a principled framework for assessing the creative capabilities of LLMs and advocates for a shift away from conventional next-token learning paradigms.
Experiments: Design a series of algorithmic tasks that require creative leaps, such as generating analogies, solving complex problems, or designing new mathematical challenges.
Compare outputs from LLMs trained with traditional next-token prediction against those trained with multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning.
Evaluate outputs using metrics for diversity and originality, such as N-gram diversity, novelty scores, and human evaluation of creativity.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Potential risks include the challenge of effectively quantifying creativity and originality, as these concepts can be subjective. Additionally, the generalizability of findings to broader real-world tasks may be limited. There is also the risk that the introduced randomness may not lead to significant improvements in all contexts.

Name: algorithmic_creativity_exploration
Title: Unleashing Algorithmic Creativity: Assessing Language Models through Multi-Token Prediction and Seed-Conditioning
Short Hypothesis: This research posits that multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning significantly enhance the algorithmic creativity of language models, allowing them to perform complex open-ended tasks that require a leap of thought, beyond the capabilities of traditional next-token prediction.
Related Work: While existing studies demonstrate the performance benefits of multi-token prediction in various contexts, there is limited exploration of its impact on creative tasks demanding abstract reasoning. This proposal uniquely focuses on quantifying creativity in LLMs through a structured evaluation of algorithmic tasks, distinguishing it from prior works that primarily emphasize performance metrics.
Abstract: This study aims to evaluate the algorithmic creativity of large language models (LLMs) by employing a novel framework of multi-token prediction (MTP) and seed-conditioning techniques. We propose a set of controlled algorithmic tasks that require a cognitive leap, such as generating analogies, constructing new mathematical problems, and creating unique narratives. We hypothesize that traditional next-token prediction is insufficient for these creative tasks, while MTP can facilitate more diverse and original outputs. Seed-conditioning, which introduces controlled randomness at the input layer, is posited as an effective mechanism to enhance this creativity without compromising coherence. Our experiments will assess outputs using metrics for originality, diversity, and human evaluation. This research will contribute to a deeper understanding of how LLMs can be harnessed for creative applications, advocating for a shift in training paradigms towards fostering algorithmic creativity.
Experiments: Design and implement a series of creative tasks that require algorithmic leaps, such as generating analogies, solving complex problems, and crafting unique narratives.
Compare outputs from LLMs trained with traditional next-token prediction against those trained with multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning across the creative tasks.
Evaluate outputs using a mix of automated metrics (e.g., N-gram diversity, novelty scores) and human evaluations focused on creativity and originality.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Challenges may arise in effectively quantifying creativity due to its subjective nature. Additionally, the generalizability of our findings to broader real-world tasks may be limited, and there is a risk that the introduced randomness may not yield improvements in all contexts.

Name: layered_creativity_in_lms
Title: Unveiling Layered Creativity: Enhancing Algorithmic Creativity in Language Models through Multi-Token Prediction and Seed-Conditioning
Short Hypothesis: This research investigates how multi-token prediction and input-layer seed-conditioning interact with specific layers of language models to enhance their algorithmic creativity in open-ended tasks, revealing insights into the architecture's role in creative output.
Related Work: While existing work has demonstrated the advantages of multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning, little has been done to analyze how these techniques interact with different layers of language model architectures. This proposal distinguishes itself by systematically exploring layer-specific impacts on creativity, which is a novel approach in the current literature.
Abstract: This study aims to deepen our understanding of algorithmic creativity in large language models (LLMs) by examining how multi-token prediction and input-layer seed-conditioning can enhance creative outputs across different layers of the model. We propose a set of structured algorithmic tasks requiring creative leaps, such as generating analogies and solving complex problems. By analyzing the performance of LLMs with varied layer configurations, we hypothesize that the combination of multi-token prediction with seed-conditioning at the input layer can significantly boost diversity and originality in outputs. Our experiments will utilize a mix of automated creativity metrics and human evaluations to assess the quality of outputs across different layers. This research advocates for a nuanced understanding of model architecture in fostering algorithmic creativity, encouraging a shift in training paradigms to optimize for creative tasks.
Experiments: Design and implement a range of creative tasks that require algorithmic leaps, such as generating analogies, constructing new mathematical problems, and crafting unique narratives.
Train LLMs using multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning, and vary layer configurations to analyze their effects on creative outputs.
Evaluate outputs using a combination of automated metrics (e.g., N-gram diversity, novelty scores) and human assessments focused on creativity and originality.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Quantifying creativity is inherently subjective, which may complicate evaluations. Additionally, the findings may not generalize well to all real-world tasks, and the interaction effects at different layers could be complex to disentangle.

Name: creativity_in_lms_redefined
Title: Redefining Algorithmic Creativity: A Novel Framework for Enhancing Language Models through Multi-Token Prediction and Seed-Conditioning
Short Hypothesis: This research aims to redefine algorithmic creativity in language models by introducing a framework that quantifies creativity through unique algorithmic tasks and investigates the impact of multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning on creative outputs.
Related Work: While existing studies have focused on enhancing performance through multi-token prediction, limited research investigates how these approaches can specifically enhance algorithmic creativity in language models. This proposal distinguishes itself by defining creativity in a structured manner and exploring unique tasks that require abstract reasoning.
Abstract: This study proposes a novel framework for evaluating and enhancing algorithmic creativity in large language models (LLMs). We define algorithmic creativity as the ability to generate novel and diverse outputs through abstract reasoning. Our framework introduces a suite of unique algorithmic tasks that require LLMs to make creative leaps, such as generating analogies and solving complex problems. We hypothesize that multi-token prediction (MTP) and seed-conditioning techniques can enhance the diversity and originality of outputs. By systematically evaluating outputs using both traditional and novel creativity metrics, we aim to provide insights into the mechanisms of creativity in LLMs. Our work advocates for a paradigm shift towards fostering algorithmic creativity in model training and application, with potential implications across educational, artistic, and scientific domains.
Experiments: Design and implement a series of unique algorithmic tasks that require LLMs to engage in abstract reasoning and creative problem-solving.
Train LLMs using traditional next-token prediction and compare their outputs with those using multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning.
Evaluate outputs using a combination of traditional metrics (e.g., N-gram diversity) and novel metrics specifically designed to capture creativity, such as uniqueness and coherence scores.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Challenges may arise in effectively quantifying creativity due to its subjective nature. The generalizability of findings to broader real-world tasks may be limited, and there is a risk that introduced randomness in seed-conditioning may not lead to significant improvements across all tasks.

Name: structured_creativity_in_lms
Title: Harnessing Structured Constraints to Enhance Algorithmic Creativity in Language Models
Short Hypothesis: This research investigates how imposing structured constraints on creative tasks influences the algorithmic creativity of language models, revealing insights into their adaptability and robustness compared to traditional prediction methods.
Related Work: Existing literature has explored multi-token prediction and seed-conditioning to enhance algorithmic creativity. However, there is limited investigation into how structured constraints can further shape the creative outputs of LLMs. This proposal distinguishes itself by systematically analyzing the impact of constraints on model performance, a perspective not widely covered in current research.
Abstract: This study aims to explore the effects of structured constraints on the algorithmic creativity of large language models (LLMs) during creative tasks. We hypothesize that introducing constraints—such as specific thematic requirements, word limits, or narrative structures—can enhance the models' ability to generate diverse and original outputs. By comparing outputs from LLMs operating under traditional next-token prediction with those subjected to multi-token prediction and structured constraints, we aim to uncover the adaptability and robustness of LLMs in the face of creative challenges. Our experiments will evaluate outputs using a mix of automated creativity metrics and human assessments, focusing on originality, coherence, and diversity. This research advocates for a deeper understanding of how structured constraints can be leveraged to foster algorithmic creativity in language models, with potential applications across various domains, including education, storytelling, and problem-solving.
Experiments: Design a series of creative tasks with varying levels of structured constraints, such as generating analogies with specific themes or crafting narratives within word limits.
Train LLMs using traditional next-token prediction and compare outputs against those using multi-token prediction with varying degrees of constraints.
Evaluate the outputs using a combination of automated metrics (e.g., N-gram diversity, coherence scores) and human evaluations focused on creativity and originality.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Challenges may arise in quantifying creativity due to its subjective nature. The generalizability of findings to broader real-world tasks may be limited, and the effects of structured constraints may not yield improvements across all contexts.
